title: EON Stream trust set (v0 — UNSTABLE)
description: The signing keys a build trusts, and the window in which it trusts each one. Clients trust more than one key at a time so rotation locks nobody out; the consequence that needs care is the other direction, where a client whose whole set has expired must refuse and say its trust data is stale rather than accept whatever it is given. v0 is explicitly unstable.

keys.description: Every key currently shipped, expired ones included. An expired key left in the set produces 'this key expired on <date>'; one dropped from the set produces only 'unknown key'. The first is a diagnosis, the second is a mystery.

keyId.description: What a signature names. Unique within the set.

purpose.description: What this key may sign. The Edu key is deliberately separate from the EON Stream module key (madde 22): an Edu build trusts the Edu key only, so a module from the open marketplace does not fail a policy check — it fails signature verification, which no setting reaches. The separation runs both ways, so an Edu-signed module cannot be installed into an open build either. An institution key is generated by the institution on its own server; the project never holds one.

notAfter.description: End of the validity window, exclusive. Must be after notBefore. Keys overlap during a rotation: the new key ships in a release, both are valid for a period, the old one expires.

comment.description: Whose key it is and where it lives. Shown to whoever asks what this build trusts.
